title: A Lent plan
hookLine: one prayer, one fast, one gift
tomorrow: what did the women do on the Saturday nobody talks about?

lines: A LIST BECOMES A GUILT TRIP.
cards: New Year's resolutions tend to come as lists: run, read, sleep more, save money, call Grandma. A few weeks later, the list is a guilt trip. Lent's plan is shorter.
On Ash Wednesday, the Gospel at Mass is Jesus in Matthew six, naming three practices and asking that each be done in secret: giving alms, praying, fasting. Three things. That's the whole plan.

teach.h: IN SECRET, NOT FOR AN AUDIENCE.
teach.b: Jesus doesn't argue for them; he assumes them. When you give alms, when you pray, when you fast. His point is how: quietly, for your Father who sees in secret, not for an audience.
When you give, he says, don't let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.

teach.h: PRAYER IS GOOD WITH FASTING AND ALMS.
teach.b: The book of Tobias, in the Catholic Bible, puts the three in one breath: "Prayer is good with fasting and alms." They hold each other up.

teach.h: ONE PRAYER, ONE FAST, ONE GIFT.
teach.b: The fast makes room, the room goes to prayer, and what you saved goes to someone else. So a Lent plan is one of each. One prayer: a set time, a psalm, a weekday Mass.
One fast: something you'll go without, small enough to keep. One gift: money, time, attention for someone who needs it.

Small enough that you could still be keeping all three on a tired Tuesday in week five. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: Lent's forty days echo Jesus's own forty days of fasting in the desert, in Matthew four.
And this was a week of seasons, so here's the whole run: the door is wide, wait at home, keep feasting, the house blessed, grow slowly, and now, three things.

how: Catholics begin Lent on Ash Wednesday and keep its three practices, prayer, fasting and almsgiving, often choosing one of each; the Ash Wednesday Gospel is Matthew 6.

o: one prayer, one fast and one gift for forty days

s: in Matthew 6, Jesus says to fast where people can see you
he says the opposite: in secret, for your Father who sees in secret.
Lent is only about giving something up
giving up is one of three. prayer and alms are the other two.
Lent's forty days echo Jesus's forty days in the desert
Matthew 4: he fasted forty days and forty nights.

games.q: your friend's whole Lent plan is to give up chocolate. going by the three things, what's missing?
o: a prayer and a gift: the fast makes room for both.
nothing: giving something up is the whole of Lent.
a harder fast, like skipping all meals on Fridays.
games.why: Matthew 6 names three: alms, prayer, fasting. the fast makes room; prayer and the gift fill it.

practice: Say your three things out loud, one short sentence each: one prayer, one fast, one gift. If any of them is too big to keep for weeks, shrink it and say it again.
Then sit with the plan for the rest of the time, holding it the way you'd hold something easy to drop.
